content.value_statement: Tailwind projects often need consistent utility patterns and responsive components. This skill provides quick references for layouts, states, forms, cards, and dark mode.
actual_capabilities: Lists Tailwind CSS responsive breakpoint prefixes and their minimum widths.
Shows common layout patterns for containers, flex rows, grids, and stacks.
Provides reusable examples for cards, buttons, inputs, navigation, forms, lists, alerts, badges, and loading states.
Includes dark mode class patterns and a simple Tailwind configuration example.
Summarizes state modifiers such as hover, focus, active, disabled, and group hover.
Explains spacing scale examples and arbitrary value syntax.
limitations: It is a reference skill, not a complete Tailwind CSS documentation replacement.
It targets Tailwind CSS version 3 and newer projects.
It does not validate generated markup in a browser.
It does not include JavaScript behavior for interactive components.

use_cases.title: Create Responsive Layouts
use_cases.description: Use breakpoint and grid patterns to design layouts that adapt across mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.

use_cases.title: Standardize UI Components
use_cases.description: Reuse consistent cards, buttons, forms, alerts, badges, and loading states across a product interface.

use_cases.title: Review Tailwind Utility Choices
use_cases.description: Compare spacing, state, dark mode, and arbitrary value patterns before editing an existing interface.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Utility Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for a common Tailwind pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Tailwind patterns skill to suggest utility classes for a responsive card with padding, shadow, and hover styling.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Tailwind patterns skill to convert this layout idea into mobile-first container, flex, and grid utility guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Component Consistency
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of repeated UI elements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these product components with the Tailwind patterns skill and align their spacing, states, borders, and responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Tailwind Interface System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a reusable interface set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Tailwind patterns skill to define a component pattern set for navigation, forms, alerts, badges, loading states, and dark mode.

output_examples.input: Request a responsive pricing card pattern.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a centered card, emphasized plan label, price hierarchy, feature list spacing, and a full-width action button.

output_examples.input: Ask how to add dark mode support to a section.
output_examples.output: The response explains class-based dark mode and pairs light background and text utilities with dark variants.

output_examples.input: Ask for loading states for a submit action.
output_examples.output: The response suggests spinner, skeleton, and disabled button patterns with clear spacing and accessible loading text.

best_practices: Start with mobile-first classes, then add breakpoint prefixes only where the layout needs to change.
Keep spacing, border radius, and shadow choices consistent across repeated components.
Pair interactive states with accessible disabled, focus, and dark mode styles.
anti_patterns: Avoid copying component snippets without adjusting content, semantics, and accessibility attributes.
Avoid using arbitrary values when the standard Tailwind scale communicates the design well.
Avoid mixing many unrelated utility styles when a reusable component pattern would be clearer.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides Tailwind utility and component patterns that can support application development.

faq.question: Which Tailwind CSS versions does it target?
faq.answer: The skill states compatibility with Tailwind CSS version 3 and newer projects.

faq.question: Can it help with responsive design?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes breakpoint prefixes and mobile-first layout examples for common screen sizes.

faq.question: Does it include dark mode guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes class-based dark mode patterns and a basic Tailwind configuration example.

faq.question: Does it run commands or install packages?
faq.answer: No. The skill files contain documentation and examples only.

faq.question: Can it replace the official Tailwind documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a quick pattern reference and check official documentation for full API details.
